sources.entry: LibreServer - Home server configuration based on Debian. (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Shell

summary.one_liner: LibreServer is a Debian-based home server configuration system for running your own internet services such as email, chat, VoIP, wikis, blogs and social networks.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes LibreServer as a small server system for running your own internet services independently. It says it includes email, chat, VoIP, wikis, blogs, social networks and more. The README says it can run on an old laptop or single board computer, and that it can also be run on an onion address. The README points to a website for installation instructions and other information, and does not include install steps itself. The metadata describes it as a home server configuration based on Debian, written in Shell and licensed under AGPL-3.0.
use_cases: self-host email for family or friends
run a personal chat or VoIP server
host a personal wiki or blog
run a private social network server
turn an old laptop into a home server
host services reachable over an onion address
how_to_run: See the project website for installation instructions (not included in the README).
stack: Matrix (Conduit server referenced in the README's chat room address)
notable: Bundles several self-hosted services (email, chat, VoIP, wikis, blogs, social networking) into one server configuration
Can run on an onion address
Designed for old laptops and single board computers
Aims for federation between personal servers
caveats: README gives no installation commands; setup details are only on the external website
Limited README detail on specific services and versions
